distinguishing_features: Uses a micro-lamella heat-transfer surface designed with controlled ice-nucleation sites.
Pins ice nucleation to designated high-shear surfaces rather than allowing stochastic nucleation throughout the flow.
Continuously detaches and disperses nascent ice into the bulk before a thick, solute-trapping layer develops.
Applies high-shear boundary-layer control specifically to freeze concentration rather than breaking up precipitated crude solids.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Prevent formation of an adherent, heat-insulating ice mass that occludes juice solutes and impedes heat and mass transfer during freeze concentration.
parsed.viable_reason: A textured, cooled microchannel operated at high wall shear can continuously nucleate, detach, and disperse ice while suppressing a thick insulating layer, although the stated Reynolds-number criterion and adhesion assumptions require practical validation.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Unlike the closest art, which shears already-precipitated solids to break a gel network, the candidate deliberately organizes ice nucleation and removes nascent crystals before they grow into a solute-trapping mass, a mechanism not obtained through routine parameter adjustment.
